Position Summary
As the Dual Special Needs Plan (DSNP) business continues to expand, we are seeking an experienced Manager, Encounter Data & State Submission Operations to lead the end-to-end management of encounter and claims data submissions to state agencies. This role requires strong knowledge of healthcare claims processing, encounter reporting, the 837 claims transaction standard, and state-specific submission requirements, with responsibility for ensuring the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of encounter data submissions. The Manager will partner closely with internal business and technical teams, as well as external vendors, to meet regulatory and operational requirements across multiple states, while demonstrating strong leadership experience managing workflows and leading, developing, and supporting teams within a healthcare operations environment.

The Manager will be responsible for ensuring the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of encounter data submissions while partnering closely with internal business and technical teams, as well as external vendors, to meet regulatory and operational requirements across multiple states.

Key Responsibilities
- Serve as the subject matter expert for state-specific encounter data submission requirements and maintain comprehensive documentation of all applicable regulations and processes.
- Lead the end-to-end management of encounter submissions, ensuring compliance with state and regulatory requirements.
- Partner with technical teams and vendors to implement, monitor, and maintain processes that support accurate encounter data reporting and submissions.
- Oversee 837 file transmission processes, ensuring files are submitted accurately, timely, and in accordance with state specifications.
- Manage state response files, reconciliation activities, and error reporting to ensure all submitted transactions are accounted for and resolved.
- Establish and maintain reporting, monitoring, and tracking processes for encounter submission performance, acceptance rates, and error trends.
- Drive root cause analysis and coordinate corrective actions to resolve encounter submission errors and improve data quality.
- Develop, document, and enhance operational processes related to encounter data management and state reporting.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Claims, IT, Compliance, Operations, Risk Adjustment, and vendor partners to ensure alignment and successful execution of encounter submission objectives.
- Support audits, regulatory reviews, and internal compliance initiatives related to encounter data submissions.
- Monitor changes in state and federal requirements and lead implementation efforts to maintain ongoing compliance.

Required Qualifications
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in healthcare claims operations, including medical claims processing and/or Medicare and Medicaid lines of business.
- At least 2 years of experience overseeing secure data transmission processes utilizing SFTP and other file transfer technologies, with responsibility for monitoring, troubleshooting, and ensuring data integrity.
- 3+ years of experience in data management, including data validation, reconciliation, reporting, and issue resolution.
- 3+ years of leadership experience with demonstrated success managing workflows and leading, developing, and supporting teams within a healthcare operations environment.

Preferred Qualifications
- 2+ years experience working with states on DSNP encounter submissions.
- 2+ years experience working with the state of Florida on encounter submissions.
- 2+ years experience with vendor management.
- Candidates located on the East Coast are strongly preferred.

Education
- Bachelor's degree preferred or a combination of professional work experience and education.

jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Oak Street Health®, a part of CVS Health, helps older adults stay healthier and live fuller lives through our 230 centers across 27 states. Our value-based care model helps us consistently deliver better patient experiences and outcomes.

As the nation’s leading health solutions company, we reach millions of Americans through our local presence, digital channels, and more than 300,000 purpose-driven colleagues — caring for people where, when, and how they choose in a way that is uniquely more connected, more convenient, and more compassionate. And we do it all with heart, each and every day.

Role Overview
As a Regional Director, Operations, you will play a critical role in supporting our Oak Street Health patients, providers and business by leading operational performance and population health execution across multiple centers within a geographic division. This role owns the delivery of key clinical, operational, patient experience, quality, utilization, and financial outcomes by ensuring that regional priorities are translated into disciplined execution across centers and care teams.

This leader reports directly to the Regional Vice President and works in close partnership with the Senior Medical Director , regional leaders, and central functional partners, including the central Population Health team. The role directly leads center operational leadership, including Practice Managers and other regional operational resources, and serves as a key cross-functional partner to clinical, service, outreach, and Treehouse teams.

Success in this role requires a leader who can drive results across a matrixed environment, build strong relationships quickly, and bring both strategic and operational rigor to a fast-paced, high-visibility setting. This individual will be accountable for improving the day-to-day performance of centers while also advancing Oak Street Health’s broader population health and value-based care priorities.

Core Responsibilities
Operational Leadership Across the Region
- Lead operational oversight and performance across multiple centers within a geography
- Ensure centers are operationally efficient and optimizing resources in service of patients
- Drive strong execution in patient experience, patient engagement, schedule management, patient responsiveness, and center-level operational performance
- Identify operational opportunities proactively and implement practical, sustainable solutions
- Support center-level leaders in problem-solving, execution discipline, and continuous improvement
- Share best practices and strengthen coordination across centers and markets

Population Health Ownership and Execution
- Own execution and ongoing refinement of population health priorities across the division
- Drive divisional performance across key population health domains, including transitions in care, pharmacy and medication adherence, HEDIS / Stars, accurate risk adjustment, preferred partner relationships, and patient engagement strategy
- Ensure Oak Street Health’s clinical and business priorities are effectively implemented at the regional and center level
- Maintain accountability for key quality, utilization, and financial performance measures tied to population health outcomes
- Translate data and organizational priorities into focused regional action plans that improve quality, cost of care, and patient outcomes

Program Implementation and Cross-Functional Leadership
- Lead implementation of centrally driven and regionally driven initiatives that improve operations and population health performance
- Partner with central functional leaders to support strategy development, program design, workflow refinement, and execution feedback
- Assess workflow impact across service, outreach, clinical, and operational teams to ensure effective implementation of new initiatives
- Serve as a regional subject matter expert on operational and population health programs, priorities, and performance opportunities
- Apply strong project management and change leadership practices to ensure initiatives are launched and sustained effectively

Leader Development and Regional Team Effectiveness
- Lead, coach, and develop Practice Managers and other regional operational leaders with clear accountability for outcomes
- Onboard, train, and support new leaders to build capability and consistency across the region
- Conduct operational reviews focused on performance, quality, patient experience, and other key metrics
- Foster a collaborative regional culture across operational and clinical teams
- Support team development and strengthen consistency across centers in how care is delivered and operations are led
- Model and reinforce Oak Street Health’s mission, culture, and standards throughout the region

Qualifications
- 5+ years of leadership experience in healthcare, population health, clinical operations, or a related field
- Multi-site leadership experience strongly preferred
- Bachelor’s degree required
- Graduate degree preferred, including MBA, MPH, or similar advanced degree
- Strong leadership and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across a matrixed organization
- Demonstrated ability to build trust and credibility with a wide range of stakeholders, including providers, care teams, operational leaders, and central partners
- Strong analytical and financial acumen, including experience using data to drive performance, develop business cases, and assess ROI
- Excellent organizational skills, sound judgment, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
- Strong communication skills and the ability to connect individual initiatives to broader organizational objectives
- High degree of independence, reliability, and execution focus in a fast-paced environment
- Quick learner who is comfortable operating in ambiguity and leading through change
- Proficiency with Excel, Google applications, and project management tools
- Willingness to travel regularly within the assigned geography
- US work authorization required

What It Means to Be Oaky
- Creating an unmatched patient experience
- Driving clinical excellence
- Taking ownership and delivering results
- Being scrappy
- Radiating positive energy
- Assuming good intentions

Oak Street Health offers colleagues the opportunity to be at the forefront of a revolution in healthcare, along with:
- A collaborative and energetic culture
- A fast-paced and innovative environment
- High levels of responsibility and opportunity for impact
- Competitive benefits, including paid vacation and sick time, retirement benefits, and health coverage

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

The Operations Manager is a member of the Store Management team, and as such, fulfills the company purpose of helping people on their path to better health by driving store execution and performance while building consumer loyalty to CVS/pharmacy through a focus on excellent customer service. Under the supervision of the Store Manager, the Operations Manager will maintain an engaged, productive store team through strong leadership, demonstrating initiative and leading by example.

The Operations Manager is responsible for supporting the Store Manager in the total leadership and strategic operation of a CVS/pharmacy store including:

- Overall store management, supervision, and policy implementation
- Sales and inventory management
- Employee staffing, training, and development
- Financial management
- Customer service leadership

Unlike the Store Manager in Training position, the Operations Manager position is not part of the CVS/pharmacy Retail Management Development Program. Operations Managers are not eligible for direct promotion to Store Manager. Candidates with a short-term goal of becoming a CVS Store Manager should instead apply for Store Manager in Training openings.
Essential Functions:
1. Management
Lead others and work effectively with store crews
Supervise, assign and direct activities of the store’s crew
Effectively communicate information to store crew and supervisors in an open and timely manner
Support Store Manager with actions plans for operational and service improvement
2. Customer Service
Assist customers with their questions, problems and complaints
Promote CVS customer service culture (greet, offer help, and thank)

Required Qualifications

- Deductive reasoning ability, advanced analytical skills and computer skills.
- Advanced communication skills, leadership, supervision, and influencing skill
- Ability to work a full-time flexible schedule, including some early morning, overnight and weekend shifts, to work overtime as needed, and to respond to urgent issues at the store when they arise

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience as a retail manager or supervisor

Education

High School diploma or equivalent preferred but not required.

Anticipated Weekly Hours
40

Time Type
Full time

Pay Range
The typical pay range for this role is:

$20.00 - $34.00
This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls.  The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.
Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments .

We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 10/31/2026

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Position Summary

The Senior Category Manager, Strategic Sourcing within the Enterprise Operations team plays a critical role in advancing CVS Health’s enterprise transformation by leading strategically important sourcing initiatives across indirect procurement. This role combines data, technology, and strong business partnership to modernize how sourcing decisions are defined, executed, and communicated. This position operates within a forward-looking procurement organization that is actively embedding digital tools, advanced analytics, and emerging AI capabilities into sourcing workflows—enabling smarter decisions, faster execution, and increased enterprise value.

Enterprise Operations, including Facilities, Construction, Loss Prevention, Architecture & Engineering, Logistics/Transportation, Distribution Center Operations, and Supply Chain Innovation, and related operational services.

Work Model: Hybrid
Candidates within commuting distance to Woonsocket, RI; Hartford, CT; Buffalo Grove, IL; will work onsite two days per week.

Key Responsibilities

Category Strategy & Management
- Develop and evolve multi‑year category strategies, leveraging market intelligence, demand analysis, total cost of ownership, and negotiation strategies to drive sustainable value and risk mitigation
- Define and lead category‑level negotiation approaches, aligning objectives, negotiation levers, and concession strategies with financial goals, market dynamics, and enterprise priorities
- Lead stakeholder and leadership reviews to align category sourcing and negotiation roadmaps with financial, operational, and enterprise strategy
- Use advanced spend and market analytics to inform negotiation planning, guide cost reduction, optimize the supply base, and unlock category value
- Advance category strategy through emerging technology and AI, applying automation and analytics to enhance negotiation insights, improve cycle times, and strengthen decision‑making

Strategic Sourcing & Negotiations
- Lead end-to-end sourcing initiatives for complex categories (RFx through contract award)
- Execute negotiations with embedded productivity, continuous improvement, and market-based pricing mechanisms
- Deliver year-over-year savings through disciplined opportunity pipelines and value tracking
- Apply competitive bidding, should-cost analysis, and total value frameworks to maximize outcomes

Stakeholder Partnership
- Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders by translating sourcing strategies into clear business results
- Drive cross-functional alignment across Finance, Legal, IT, Contracting, and Operations
- Communicate insights and recommendations in concise, executive-ready formats

Team Leadership & Development
- Develop sourcing talent in analytics, negotiation, and sourcing methodologies
- Foster a high-performance culture grounded in accountability, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making

Key Competencies
- Strategic mindset connecting analytics, technology, and business outcomes
- Proven ability to lead sourcing initiatives end-to-end in evolving or transformational environments
- Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional influence
- Comfort navigating ambiguity and driving structure through data and process discipline
- Interest in leveraging automation, advanced analytics, and AI to elevate sourcing effectiveness

Qualifications
- 7–10 years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, or procurement
- Proven leadership of complex RFx events, negotiations, and end-to-end sourcing
- Track record of sustained year-over-year cost savings and strong analytical skills
- Experience with indirect categories, digital procurement tools, and/or professional certification

Education
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience ( 4 years)
MBA or advanced degree preferred

jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary
Lead Director, Senior Category Manager, Photo and Services
Are you passionate about building customer focused assortments, driving innovation, and leading high-impact retail strategies that shape how customers shop every day?

This is an exciting leadership opportunity to shape the future of the Photo and Services business at CVS Health. As Lead Director, Senior Category Manager, you will lead a highly visible, customer-cherished portfolio with responsibility for driving sales, margin growth, customer engagement, vendor strategy, and omnichannel merchandising experiences across stores and digital channels.

In this role, you will set the strategic direction for the category, translate customer and market insights into actionable business plans, and partner cross-functionally to deliver growth, innovation, and differentiated experiences for CVS Health customers. You will also lead and develop a team of Category Merchants and Analysts, building talent, accountability, and a strong culture of performance.
Our Heart At Work Behaviors™ support this purpose. We want everyone who works at CVS Health to feel empowered by the role they play in transforming our culture and accelerating our ability to innovate.

In this role, you will:
- Deliver sales and margin goals by attaining market share and thoughtfully managing all lines of the category P&L
- Lead and manage large vendor relationships, including joint business planning development and vendor negotiations to secure innovation, funding, service levels, differentiated assortments and profitable growth.
- Develop and implement category plans (i.e., plan optimal SKU mix; ExtraCare loyalty program; weekly, seasonal, annual promotional programs) for merchandising programs that reflect deep personal knowledge of our businesses, customers and client.
- Initiate and execute strategic promotional strategies and marketing plans by influencing and aligning CVS partners (e.g., Inventory, Pricing, Promotion, Finance, Store Brands, Store Design, IT, Tech Platform, Store Operations, and Loyalty) and supplier partners to execute category priorities.
- Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team with clear goals, accountability, and a strong pipeline of future merchandising talent.
- Leverage customer, loyalty, market, and competitive insights to identify growth opportunities, inform assortment, pricing, promotion, and merchandising decisions, and continually sustain a strong understanding of current competition.
- Contribute to the development and execution of General Merchandising initiatives.

Required Qualifications
- 10+ years category management and/or direct spend experience, with a track record of meeting, or exceeding, financial objectives and P&L ownership.

- Demonstrated ability to translate customer, market, and competitive insights into actionable category strategies.

- Proven track record of influencing others with and without authority

- Experience building high-performing, successful teams developing key talent.

- Experience leading under pressure, adapting quickly to changing dynamics, and developing solutions that meet the needs of multiple business stakeholders.

- Ability to lead through ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced retail environment.

The Inventory Analytics & Governance Manager is an individual contributor role responsible for supporting Inventory, Data Analytics, DC, and Merchandising partners through the full lifecycle of inventory initiatives, from concept and pilot through testing, implementation, and benefit realization. This role applies a structured decision-making framework to evaluate inventory changes, ensuring parameter updates, policy decisions, and system enhancements are evidence-based, financially sound, and fully traceable.

The role serves as a subject matter expert on inventory planning processes and technologies, bridging internally developed applications and enterprise planning platforms such as Blue Yonder to ensure alignment across tools, processes, and business objectives. This position also owns the development and maintenance of the team's SOP library, governance standards, and supporting documentation.

In addition, the Manager leads training and knowledge transfer efforts, establishing clear operating models, defining decision rights, and determining when partner teams can operate independently versus when F&R engagement is required.

Key Responsibilities:
Inventory Change Governance & Rubric
- Own and maintain the rubric used to evaluate inventory changes — defining the evidence standards, financial thresholds, and approval criteria required before changes move to pilot or implementation.

- Maintain an audit trail of inventory parameter changes, policy decisions, and test outcomes, ensuring traceability and accountability across the planning cycle.

- Partner with inventory planners, DC, and Merchandising teams to ensure changes to planning parameters (e.g., Blue Yonder settings, WOS targets, safety stock) follow established governance protocols.

Analytics & Experimentation
- Support inventory, DC, and Merchandising partners from concept through implementation: scope the problem, design the test or pilot, define measurement methodology, track results, and synthesize findings into a clear recommendation.

- Build and maintain analytical frameworks and models that support repeatable decision-making on inventory policies and system changes.

Financial Tracking & Alignment
- Track inventory investment implications of active tests and implemented changes against expected outcomes.

- Translate inventory decisions into financial language for leadership visibility — connecting parameter changes to working capital, margin, and service level impacts.

- Partner with Finance, DC, Merchandising, and Inventory Planning teams to ensure inventory change decisions align with broader financial targets.

- Serve as a connector across the inventory tool landscape — developing a working understanding of how internally developed applications and enterprise planning platforms (including Blue Yonder) interact and complement each other.

- Identify gaps or friction points where tool connectivity is breaking down and surface recommendations to the F&R team and technology partners.

- Develop and maintain a library of SOPs, process documentation, and decision frameworks covering inventory governance, change management, and analytical methodologies.
